direction: BTC/ETH daily cross-sectional relative-strength rotation with an absolute momentum hurdle
hypothesis: When BTC and ETH have divergent trailing returns, holding the stronger asset may capture relative momentum; an absolute hurdle can keep the account in cash when both trends are weak. Correlated crypto assets may limit the benefit, and daily rotation costs may erase gross spread.
rule: At UTC daily decision index i use only completed close C[i-1]. Compute simple close-to-close return r_a=C_a[i-1]/C_a[i-1-L]-1 for BTC and ETH. Let winner be BTC on ties (rBTC >= rETH), otherwise ETH. Target the winner only if max(rBTC,rETH) is strictly greater than hurdle; otherwise target cash. Rebalance only when target differs from current holding. Execute after signal availability at next UTC day 00:01 one-minute open. A switch sells the old asset first and then buys the new asset from remaining cash at the same recorded timestamp, charging both legs. Rejected sells preserve the old holding; rejected buys leave cash and are reconsidered at the next daily decision. No shorting, leverage, simultaneous holdings, rebalance while winner is unchanged, cash yield, or pre-OOS position replay.
allocation: One independent $2,000 account per parameter configuration; target is 100% of remaining account cash in one BTC or ETH asset, or 100% cash under the absolute hurdle. No raw BTC/ETH weights, cross-configuration transfer, or cash interest.

gates.interpretation: Pass denotes this repeated-history validation screen only; it is not independent out-of-sample or live-profit evidence.

literature.citation: Gbadebo, A.D. (2026). Momentum Trading in Cryptocurrencies: A Comparative Study of Time-Series and Cross-Sectional Strategies. Buhalterinės apskaitos teorija ir praktika, 33, 1–25. DOI:10.15388/batp.2026.1.
literature.use: The paper compares time-series and cross-sectional momentum on eight major cryptoassets (2020-01 to 2025-10), reporting high correlation and larger drawdowns for cross-sectional allocation. This smaller BTC/ETH long-only rotation with an absolute-return gate is a predeclared adaptation, not a reproduction.

data.source: Binance spot 1m OHLCV, normalized closed bars
data.reuse_disclosure: The interval is repeatedly used development/validation history and is not an untouched final holdout.

walk_forward.parameter_fit: None; all strategy parameters fixed before evaluation. Prior closes are used only for the declared momentum lookback and cost estimates. OOS starts with $2,000 cash and carries one position or cash continuously across folds.

execution.reference_price: Next UTC day 00:01 one-minute open. Switching first liquidates the held asset, then invests remaining cash in the new leader using the same observed historical timestamp; each leg incurs its own cost. Historical L2 is unavailable; spread/impact are estimated, not an exchange fill guarantee.

costs.impact_formula: 0.5 * sample std(previous 20 complete UTC daily log returns) * sqrt(order budget / mean quote turnover(previous 20 complete UTC days))

prior_results.finding: All 16 initial registry entries have actual result evidence; no exact missing-result initial configuration to rerun.
